bc_the_main_event.blurb: A small steep sport wall in Cheakamus Canyon, between Squamish and Whistler, on the Chek hillside. It holds six bolted routes, running from one 5.8 through a pair of 5.10s to a trio of 5.11s, so it suits climbers warming up and those pushing into the low 5.11 range alike. The wall is popular partly because it keeps climbing in wet weather, and the rock offers good friction. The walk goes south from the upper lot, past two other sectors, and ends shortly before another wall.

bc_the_substation.blurb: A short, steep sport crag in Cheakamus Canyon, north of Squamish, and one of the newer bolted sectors on the Chek hillside. Six bolted lines go up the wall, grading mostly from 5.10 to 5.12, with half of them in the 5.12 range. The routes are described as burly power-endurance climbing, so expect sustained effort on steep rock rather than gentle warm-ups.

bc_sector_4.blurb: Sector 4 is a sport wall on Nathan's Wall near Spillimacheen in the BC Rockies, at roughly 900 m elevation. All six routes sit in the 5.10 range, from 5.10b to 5.10d, which makes it a good grade for climbers settling into the area's style. The holds are small but the moves are not described as desperate, and the wall is the first one the approach trail reaches. Nathan's Wall as a whole is made of short, sharp routes that reward good technique and finger strength.

bc_school_yard.blurb: A short, beginner-friendly crag in the South Cliffs at Mt Wells, near Victoria on Vancouver Island. Six routes, four of them sport and two trad, all fall between 5.6 and 5.8, making it a handy place to learn leading or to teach someone to rappel. The rock is slabby, with an occasional loose spot, and the ground at the base is clean. It sits above and south of the Snooze, another sector in the South Cliffs.

bc_upper_headwall.blurb: The Upper Headwall is the tall wall of Marble Canyon, a limestone canyon in the Pavilion Mountains of south-central British Columbia, northwest of Cache Creek. The headwall stands about 500 m high on top of a lower apron, with a treed terrace between the two. Six long multi-pitch routes, a mix of trad and sport and some with aid, run from 5.8 to 5.10d. Rock quality varies between solid grey stone and crumbly red stone, so strong route-finding and a helmet are worthwhile, and be ready to rappel.
